ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary federal AML/CFT legislation is the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184. The Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers the regime. For a federal corporation, the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, including sections 21.1 to 21.303, requires a register of individuals with significant control. For an Alberta corporation, the Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c. B-9, including its beneficial-ownership and transparency-register provisions and applicable regulations, requires maintenance of a register of individuals with significant control. Alberta corporations must also comply with the Corporate Registry requirements administered under the Alberta Business Corporations Act and related regulations. The Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), the Excise Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15, and applicable provincial tax statutes govern tax registration, reporting, and audit disclosure.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or Certificate of Amalgamation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporations Canada or Alberta Corporate Registry, depending on the selected incorporation jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Canadian incorporation documents generally require neither notarization nor apostille for Canadian use. For presentation abroad, authentication and apostille are obtained from the competent Canadian authority under the destination state's requirements; consular legalization applies where the destination state is not covered by the Hague Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status or Certificate of Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporations Canada or Alberta Corporate Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication and apostille through the competent Canadian authentication authority, or consular legalization where required by the receiving state. A recent certificate is normally requested for KYC purposes.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation and Corporate Profile Report
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporations Canada or Alberta Corporate Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication and apostille, or consular legalization, only where required by the receiving authority, bank, investor, or foreign notary.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Register of Individuals with Significant Control and UBO Declaration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified corporate copy, notarization, apostille, or consular legalization may be required by the foreign recipient. The underlying identity documents must be authenticated in their country of issuance if requested.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or government-issued identity document of each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Government authority of the document holder's country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized true copy followed by Hague Apostille where the issuing state is a Hague Apostille Convention party; otherwise consular legalization through the issuing state's authority and the relevant Canadian or destination-state consulate.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or corporate registry extract for each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, depending on the issuing jurisdiction and receiving authority.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution, Power of Attorney, or Incumbency Certificate authorizing incorporation and banking
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relevant corporate shareholder or newly incorporated Canadian corporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execution before a notary where required by the recipient, followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization according to the receiving jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Banks, regulated financial institutions, tax authorities, auditors, or the relevant individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copies and, where demanded by the regulated institution or foreign authority, notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and before opening payment or banking accounts, screen all founders, directors, officers, authorized signatories, shareholders, UBOs, intermediaries, and material counterparties against United Nations Security Council sanctions implemented in Canada, Canadian domestic sanctions under the United Nations Act, the Special Economic Measures Act, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), applicable Canadian terrorist listings, and relevant foreign lists including OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists. Conduct PEP, head-of-international-organization, family-member, and close-associate screening under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and Regulations. Resolve name matches using date of birth, nationality, address, corporate role, and documentary evidence. Apply enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth verification, ongoing monitoring, and suspicious transaction escalation where a PEP, sanctions concern, adverse media issue, high-risk jurisdiction, opaque ownership chain, nominee arrangement, or unusual payment pattern is identified. A Canadian corporation is not automatically a FINTRAC reporting entity merely because it produces or distributes digital content; payment processors, banks, money-services businesses, and other covered institutions retain their own AML obligations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_identification_rules: Identify each individual who directly or indirectly owns or controls 25 percent or more of voting rights or 25 percent or more of the fair market value of shares, and each individual who exercises control in fact, alone or jointly. Trace ownership through every corporate, trust, partnership, nominee, contractual, voting, or family arrangement until natural persons are identified. Record names, dates of birth, latest known residential addresses, nationality or jurisdiction of residence, and the nature and extent of control. If no individual satisfies the ownership or control tests, record the individual or individuals who exercise directorship or equivalent senior management control, with a documented reason.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.nominee_and_layered_ownership_controls: Nominee shareholders, nominee directors, bearer instruments, undisclosed agency arrangements, unexplained intercompany loans, circular ownership, and shareholder agreements that obscure control require enhanced due diligence and documentary verification. Nominee arrangements do not replace the obligation to identify the controlling natural person.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.record_retention: Corporate beneficial-ownership records should be kept current and retained for the period required by the applicable corporate statute. Reporting entities subject to the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act generally retain required client-identification and transaction records for at least five years, subject to the applicable record category and regulatory rule.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry through Alberta.ca and an authorized Alberta registry agent; for federal incorporation, Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: An Alberta corporation may use an English, French, or combined English-French corporate name. The corporate name must comply with the Alberta Business Corporations Act and regulations, must not be confusing with an existing corporate name or trade name, and must not be misleading or objectionable. A distinctive element, descriptive element, and corporate legal element such as Inc., Incorporated, Corp., Corporation, Ltd., or Limited are normally used. A translated or alternate-language form should be separately cleared and registered where it will be used as a corporate name. Non-Latin characters and transliterations should be confirmed with the registry agent before filing. Federal corporations must comply with the Canada Business Corporations Act and Corporations Canada name rules, including the NUANS-based distinctiveness review where applicable.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying government sponsorship, regulated financial activity, a professional designation, or a public institution
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain a current Alberta NUANS or equivalent name-search report where required, submit the proposed name through an Alberta registry agent, and retain the search report, rejected-name notice, and supporting distinctiveness evidence. If rejected, determine whether the refusal is based on confusing similarity, prohibited wording, misleading implication, lack of consent, or incomplete documentation. Revise the name or obtain written consent and regulatory approval where permitted. Request written reasons from the registry agent or Corporate Registry, submit a correction or reconsideration request with the supporting report and consents, and escalate an unresolved statutory decision through the available Alberta administrative-law review or judicial-review process. A rejection should not be bypassed by filing substantially the same name through another channel. The filing deadline must be checked because NUANS reports and reservation periods are time-limited; a 90-day period is commonly used for name-search validity, while the operative reservation period may depend on the filing product and registry channel.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.name_clearance_due_diligence: Search Alberta Corporate Registry, Corporations Canada, Canadian trademarks through the Canadian Trademarks Database, relevant domain-name registries, app stores, social-media platforms, and major common-law markets. A corporate-name approval does not create trademark rights or establish freedom to operate. Obtain a Canadian trademark clearance opinion before investing in the vertical micro-drama brand.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.industry_specific_name_risk: A streaming or production name must not imply that the corporation is a broadcaster, telecom carrier, financial institution, public authority, educational institution, or licensed professional body. The proposed name should avoid terms suggesting exclusive regulatory status or government affiliation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in Alberta is mandatory for an Alberta corporation and must be a physical location capable of receiving legal documents; a post-office box alone is insufficient. A commercial registered-agent or serviced-office arrangement may be acceptable if it provides a real physical address, document-receipt capability, and corporate-record access as required by law. A purely virtual address with no responsible personnel, no document controls, and no evidence of actual operations is unsuitable for bank, payment-processor, tax, or AML onboarding. The digital-content production and distribution activity does not ordinarily require a dedicated studio at incorporation, but the corporation should maintain evidence of management, production contracts, intellectual-property ownership, platform agreements, accounting records, and Canadian decision-making where Canadian commercial substance is represented.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No Alberta authority publishes a reliable industry-specific inspection percentage. For a new low-risk digital-media corporation with complete filings, a verifiable registered office, transparent UBOs, and no regulated financial activity, the practical risk of an unannounced corporate-registry inspection is low and estimated at below 10 percent annually; the risk can materially increase if there are complaints, suspected fraud, false-address indicators, tax irregularities, sanctions concerns, unexplained ownership, or inconsistent information. Banks, payment processors, tax authorities, and law-enforcement bodies may conduct separate verification or request documentary and video evidence without an on-site visit.
substance_controls: Maintain the registered office and corporate records at a verifiable physical location.
Appoint directors who satisfy the selected incorporation statute and document their actual roles.
Maintain written IP assignments, production agreements, platform terms, licensing records, and rights-clearance files.
Use dedicated corporate bank and payment accounts and reconcile Apple, Google, Stripe, and other platform settlements.
Document Canadian tax residency analysis, management location, permanent-establishment exposure, and cross-border withholding-tax treatment.
Implement privacy, consumer-protection, advertising, copyright, music, performer, and child-safety controls where the content or audience requires them.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.regulatory_scope_assessment: Production and global distribution of vertical micro-dramas and operation of a short-drama streaming application generally does not require a general Alberta production licence or securities, banking, insurance, or money-services licence. Separate obligations may arise under the Copyright Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-42, the Personal Information Protection Act, SA 2003, c. P-6.5, the federal Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act where applicable, the Competition Act, the Online News Act where applicable, consumer-protection laws, privacy and youth-protection requirements, and platform-specific app-store rules. Payment processing through Stripe or app stores should not be structured as the corporation independently providing money-transfer or stored-value services without regulatory review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA) – ss. 9 (incorporation), 10 (articles), 16 (certificate of incorporation), 25 (share consideration), 101 (registered office and records office), 106 (directors), 114 (annual returns), 122 (officers), 137 (resolutions in writing).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry Division, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Government of Alberta; electronic filing through the Alberta Corporate Registration System (ACRS).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation – Form 1 under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), together with Form 2 (Notice of Address) and Form 4 (Director Consents/Notice).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the ABCA; shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine (s. 25(1)(b)). No escrow account is required by statute, but the subscribed consideration must be funded into the corporate bank account prior to commencement of commercial operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE DIRECTORS OF THE CORPORATION

RESOLVED THAT:
1. The Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation of the Corporation, issued by the Alberta Corporate Registry pursuant to the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), are hereby approved, ratified and adopted as the Corporation's constating documents.
2. The incorporator's subscription for 10,000 common shares at CAD 0.01 per share is accepted, and such shares are allotted, issued and declared fully paid and non-assessable.
3. The registered office in Alberta is established at the address recorded with the Registry, and the records office is placed at such address.
4. The following persons are appointed directors: [Name of Director A], [Name of Director B].
5. The following persons are appointed officers: [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary, [Name] as Treasurer.
6. The fiscal year-end of the Corporation shall be December 31 in each year.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation of Proposed Corporate Name (NUANS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction) via the Alberta Corporate Registration System (ACRS) or an authorized corporate search house.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) search for the proposed name, e.g., '[Applicant] Micro-Drama Productions Inc.' Submit the request electronically via ACRS or an approved search provider and obtain the NUANS discrimination report verifying no confusingly similar corporate name exists in the Alberta database. The NUANS report is valid for 90 days and must accompany the Articles of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search request form (ACRS or search house)
Proposed corporate name with legal element (Limited, Ltd., Incorporated, Inc., or Corp.)
Applicant/incorporator identification and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the Corporate Registry will state written reasons; the applicant may resubmit using up to five alternative names within the 90-day NUANS validity, or request a formal reconsideration supported by a letter of consent from any conflicting name holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Registry Division, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction – Alberta Corporate Registration System (ACRS), online e-filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) in ACRS, including the NUANS report reference, registered office and records office address in Alberta, authorized share structure (e.g., unlimited common shares of one class), restrictions on share transfers (if any), maximum number of directors, and any business restrictions. Confirm at least one director is Alberta-resident and at least one director is Canadian-resident (ABCA s. 106(4)). Attach signed consents to act of each director. Pay the statutory filing fee electronically and e-sign with a valid corporate access credential.
required_dossiers: Form 1 – Articles of Incorporation (Alberta)
NUANS name search report (not older than 90 days)
Form 2 – Notice of Address of Registered Office and Records Office
Form 4 / Director Consent – Notice and consent of each director
Statement of Alberta/Canadian residency for each director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Corporate Registry issues a query or rejection (e.g., defective director consent, name conflict, incomplete address), correct and resubmit the deficient schedules within 15 days; if rejected, re-file electronically with the applicable refiling fee. A compliance officer may provide written reasons and a simplified resubmission path.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Access Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, ACRS electronically issues the Certificate of Incorporation (Form 3) and assigns the unique Corporate Access Number (CAN). Download, archive and reproduce the Certificate for banking, CRA registration, payment processors (Stripe, Apple, Google), and municipal film offices. Verify the CAN is active by running an Alberta corporate standing search.
required_dossiers: Electronic Certificate of Incorporation (ACRS download)
Corporate Access Number (CAN)
Corporate standing search / company extract (if requested by banks or CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate contains errors, apply for a certificate of correction under the ABCA within 30 days of issuance; the Registry will issue a corrected certificate without invalidating the incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Governance – First Board Resolution, By-laws, Share Subscription, Registered Office Adoption and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or adopt written resolutions in lieu of meeting (ABCA s. 137). Ratify the pro-forma First Board Resolution set forth in this dossier: approve the Certificate and Articles; accept the incorporator's share subscription and allot shares; adopt By-law No. 1; designate the registered office and records office; appoint directors and officers; approve opening a corporate bank account; and authorize management to execute micro-drama distribution agreements and payment-rail merchant accounts (Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, Stripe).
required_dossiers: Pro-forma First Board Resolution (included in this dossier)
By-law No. 1 – General Operating By-law
Share subscription agreement and share certificates
Executed consent to act for each director
Registered office and records office instrument (Form 2)
Banking resolution and KYC/UBO forms for corporate account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum cannot be obtained, obtain written waivers from absent directors or call a special meeting on 24 hours' notice (ABCA s. 128(2)); if a director ceases to act, fill the vacancy by board appointment or call a shareholders' meeting to ratify.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Registration – Business Number, Corporate Income Tax, GST/HST and Payroll Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO), integrated with the Alberta Corporate Tax registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register through the CRA Business Registration Online using the Corporate Access Number (CAN) and director/officer information. Obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts: RC0001 (corporate income tax), RT0001 (GST/HST), and, if applicable, RP0001 (payroll). GST/HST registration is mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 over any four consecutive calendar quarters; the micro-drama streaming app collecting subscription revenue via Stripe, Apple IAP, and Google Play Billing will require GST/HST collection and remittance at 5% in Alberta (no provincial sales tax).
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Access Number
Form RC1 or BRO online registration request
Director/officer names, addresses and substantive identification
Corporate registered office address
Estimated revenue and date of commencement of commercial activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If BRO identity verification fails, contact the CRA Business Window (1-800-959-5525), provide the CAN and a corporate standing search from the Alberta Registry, and submit Form RC1A; once identity is confirmed, the BN is issued retroactively to the filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Annual Return Compliance, Municipal Filming Permits and Workers' Compensation Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (ACRS); City of Calgary Film Office / City of Edmonton Film Office; Workers' Compensation Board – Alberta (WCB-AB).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Alberta annual return within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation (ABCA s. 114) and keep director/officer information current via Form 4. For physical production activities, obtain a municipal filming location permit for each shoot location in Calgary or Edmonton, maintain production insurance, and register with WCB-AB for all employees and crew. Secure an occupancy and fire safety certificate for studio premises from the local authority. If the OTT streaming service qualifies as an online undertaking, monitor and comply with the CRTC online streaming registration framework under the Broadcasting Act (Online Streaming Act).
required_dossiers: Annual return form (ACRS electronic filing)
Form 4 – Notice of Change of Directors (as applicable)
Municipal filming location permit application and certificate of insurance
WCB-AB registration and clearance letter
Occupancy/fire safety certificate from the municipal fire department
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is filed late, pay the late-filing fee and file immediately; if the corporation is administratively dissolved for non-compliance, apply for revival under the ABCA revival provisions and pay all arrears before resuming operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: City of Calgary Film Office / City of Edmonton Film Office (municipal filming permits and location approvals); Travel Alberta – Alberta Film Commission (industry support and incentives); Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC) (optional online streaming undertaking registration under the Broadcasting Act).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Film and Video Production Location Permit; Business Premises Occupancy Permit; optional CRTC Online Streaming Undertaking Registration under the Broadcasting Act.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) – Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA), RSA 2000, c E-12.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – a vertical micro-drama production studio and OTT streaming business is not an activity listed under the EPEA mandatory environmental impact assessment list. No full EIA report is required. A Code-of-Practice registration may apply only if the studio generates significant wastewater discharge or hazardous waste beyond municipal thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Municipal sewer-use bylaw standards: pH 6.0–11.0, BOD ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 150 mg/L; no significant VOC or stationary air emission permits triggered for digital content production. Electronic waste and e-media must be disposed through the Alberta Recycling Management Authority (ARMA) or approved municipal e-waste programs. If backup generators or data-center cooling systems are installed, comply with CEPA 1999 refrigerant containment and EPEA cooling water discharge standards (temperature ≤ 25°C prior to discharge).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain from the local fire department an occupancy and fire safety certificate for the studio/office premises under the Safety Codes Act (Alberta Fire Code), covering means of egress, fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, fire alarm maintenance, and structural load compliance. Comply with the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Act including hazard assessment, WHMIS, and workplace security. Register with Workers' Compensation Board – Alberta (WCB-AB) and obtain a clearance letter for all employees and production crew before principal photography commences.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the Business Registration Online portal and My Business Account portal. Alberta corporate registrations are administered separately by Alberta Corporate Registry, while federal income tax and GST administration is generally performed by the CRA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate or register the corporation federally or in Alberta and obtain the certificate of incorporation or registration. 2. Apply to the CRA for a Business Number (BN) using Business Registration Online, Form RC1, or the CRA non-resident registration process. A non-resident corporation without a Canadian corporate registration may apply directly for a BN and relevant program accounts. 3. Open the applicable CRA program accounts, including Corporation Income Tax (RC), GST/HST (RT), payroll deductions (RP), and import-export (RM), as required. 4. Register for GST/HST when the statutory threshold is exceeded or voluntarily register before that time. 5. Appoint an authorized representative or Canadian service contact where required for CRA communications. 6. Maintain the BN, legal name, registered address, directors, accounting period, ownership information, and filing status consistently across CRA and corporate-registry records. A Canadian corporation generally uses its nine-digit BN and associated program-account suffixes as its principal tax identifiers; a non-resident corporation may also require a CRA-issued non-resident tax account and, where applicable, a Canadian tax identification number for treaty or withholding administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian corporations are generally taxable entities and do not have a United States-style check-the-box election to become disregarded entities or partnerships. A corporation may qualify as a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC), public corporation, or other corporate category based on statutory facts rather than a general elective classification. Available elections are transaction-specific and may include subsection 85(1) or 85(2) rollover elections, section 86 share-reorganization elections, capital-cost allowance elections, GST/HST reporting-period and accounting-method elections, and treaty-based elections or relief claims. Canadian anti-hybrid mismatch rules can deny deductions or impose income inclusions where specified hybrid arrangements produce deduction or inclusion mismatches; they do not provide a general elective hybrid entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), administered federally by the Canada Revenue Agency. Alberta does not impose a general provincial sales tax; taxable supplies in Alberta are generally subject to 5% GST only, subject to place-of-supply, zero-rating, exemption, and special non-resident digital-economy rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, excluding zero-rated supplies, measured under the GST/HST small-supplier rules. Registration is generally required when the threshold is exceeded in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters. Voluntary registration is permitted before the threshold is reached, subject to the applicable conditions and ongoing compliance obligations. Separate rules may apply to non-resident suppliers of digital products or services to Canadian consumers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Alberta do not generally require real-time electronic invoice clearance, government-issued digital invoice stamping, or universal tax-invoice API transmission for ordinary business-to-business GST transactions. Registered suppliers must issue compliant GST/HST invoices or receipts containing prescribed information, including supplier identity and GST/HST registration number where applicable, consideration, tax amount or tax calculation, tax rate, invoice date, and sufficient transaction detail. Electronic invoices and electronic records are generally acceptable if they remain accessible, reliable, readable, and capable of supporting audit verification. Electronic filing through CRA online services is required or strongly encouraged for specified registrants and returns, but it is not a real-time invoice-clearance regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada are generally zero-rated where the statutory GST export conditions are satisfied, including delivery or making the goods available outside Canada and retention of evidence establishing export. Services supplied to non-residents may be zero-rated only where a specific Excise Tax Act provision applies; non-resident status alone is insufficient. Relevant rules may cover services performed wholly outside Canada, certain advisory or professional services supplied to non-residents, qualifying services in respect of goods situated outside Canada, and other prescribed categories. Electronically supplied streaming, application, and digital-content services must be analyzed under the applicable place-of-supply and digital-economy rules; customer location, billing address, payment information, IP or device indicators, contractual rights, and the nature of the supply should be documented. Input tax credits or GST refunds require valid supporting documentation, commercial-use nexus, and compliance with the applicable limitation and documentary rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian export declaration or applicable electronic export-reporting record, including the relevant Canada Border Services Agency or Statistics Canada filing evidence where required
Commercial invoice and purchase or distribution agreement identifying the recipient, goods or rights supplied, consideration, and destination
Bill of lading, airway bill, courier record, freight forwarder record, or equivalent transport document
Proof of delivery or proof that the goods were made available outside Canada
Customs import record, destination-country import clearance, or other independent evidence of entry outside Canada where available

For services and digital supplies: contract, customer non-resident evidence, customer location and billing records, platform logs, delivery records, usage records, and evidence supporting the applicable zero-rating provision
GST/HST invoices, general-ledger records, bank statements, payment records, and input-tax-credit documentation
Evidence of refunds, chargebacks, platform settlements, and intermediary or marketplace reporting where Apple, Google, Stripe, or another payment intermediary is involved
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days. A Canadian exporter may generally retain or receive proceeds through foreign accounts, subject to ordinary income-tax, transfer-pricing, foreign-reporting, anti-money-laundering, sanctions, and exchange-control rules; Canada generally has no comprehensive foreign-exchange control regime imposing a universal repatriation deadline. CRA may deny zero-rating, assess unremitted GST, deny input tax credits, assess interest, and apply gross-negligence or other statutory penalties where export evidence is inadequate or the zero-rating claim is incorrect. False statements, wilful evasion, fraud, or deliberately altered records may result in substantial civil penalties, prosecution, fines, and imprisonment under the Excise Tax Act and Income Tax Act. Where a refund or input tax credit was improperly obtained, the amount may be reassessed and recovered with applicable interest and penalties. Records should generally be retained for at least six years from the end of the relevant reporting period, subject to longer periods for unresolved objections, appeals, or specified circumstances.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), acting under the Bank of Canada Act as the central monetary authority; Canada maintains no statutory exchange-control regime, and foreign-exchange policy is administered by the Department of Finance Canada with prudential supervision of authorized banks by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); cross-border currency and monetary-instrument reporting is enforced by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current account and capital account. The Canadian dollar (CAD) floats freely and is internationally deliverable; there are no restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, or capital repatriation by non-resident shareholders. The only legal frictions are fiscal and reporting in nature: Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident investors is 25% statutory, reducible to 5–15% under applicable income tax treaties, and FINTRAC cross-border reporting applies to currency transactions and wire transfers above CAD 10,000. For a vertical micro-drama distributor monetizing through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, foreign subscription revenue settled by app-store aggregators is freely credited to CAD accounts and convertible into USD, EUR, KRW, or any other market currency without central-bank approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory obligation to surrender export proceeds, no mandatory timeline for repatriation, and no required conversion ratio for export receipts of digital content or any other goods or services. The Alberta corporation may lawfully maintain foreign-currency accounts (USD, EUR, CNY, KRW) at Canadian banks, or with approved foreign dealers, and may retain export earnings offshore. Only FINTRAC wire-reporting and general corporate tax filing obligations attach to such proceeds; no foreign-exchange surrender certificate or central-bank approval is required.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Global Transfer Account
Operational Account and Commercial Foreign Exchange Account
Operational Account and U.S. Dollar Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operating Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium (conditional). Canada does not recognize the European EMI (Electronic Money Institution) licence class, and an offshore EMI holding funds for an Alberta company cannot lawfully operate as a deposit-taking bank under the Bank Act. Foreign digital providers such as Wise, Payoneer, and Airwallex are permissible only as low-value payout and disbursement conduits behind a primary OSFI-regulated Schedule I bank account; funds must not be permanently held at the EMI. New registration obligations under the Retail Payment Activities Act (administered by the Bank of Canada, in force 2024–2025) apply to payment service providers touching Canadian retail users. Therefore, the primary treasury wallet must remain at a Canadian regulated bank, with EMIs restricted to cross-border creator/production-studio disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandated for at least one director or signing officer. Alberta Schedule I banks ordinarily require authorized signatories who are Canadian residents to attend a branch in person for identity verification and signature specimen execution; non-resident directors may be verified through a Canadian notary or at a Canadian embassy/consulate with certified true copies and legalized documentation. Remote video onboarding is accepted by select banks (e.g., RBC, BMO) for the entity and for foreign directors in recognized low-risk jurisdictions, subject to apostilled corporate records and enhanced due diligence. Practical mandate: maintain at least one Canada-resident director or officer who can physically attend the branch; non-resident beneficial owners need not appear if their identity is supported by certified copies and a FINTRAC-compliant beneficial-ownership register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity arising from non-resident shareholders, including offshore or Asian holding-company structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized certificate of incorporation and articles; current certificate of incumbency; Alberta corporate registry search report (CORES); register of directors and registered office; signed FINTRAC-compliant Alberta Business Corporations Act transparency register disclosing all individuals with significant control; income-tax residency certificates (NR301 or equivalent) for each non-resident shareholder; bank reference letter from the beneficial owner's home institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained high-volume inbound subscription revenue settled through app-store aggregators (Apple, Google) without matching contractual evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple Developer Program Paid Applications Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement; monthly app-store settlement and payout statements; revenue reconciliation ledger tying store-reported gross billings to bank deposits; audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements; underlying content-licensing and distribution agreements evidencing the commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring wire transfers to production studios and cast/crew in higher-risk jurisdictions (e.g., Hong Kong, Singapore, South Korea) with insufficient commercial documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed production service agreements with itemized deliverables and payment schedules; aligned invoices; cast and crew contracts; intellectual-property assignment agreements; procurement and approval treasury policy requiring dual sign-off; trackable project-level cost breakdowns demonstrating that outbound wires trace to identifiable productions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Chargeback volatility and rapid refund flows (typical of digital content subscriptions) triggering payment-fraud red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chargeback register and refund policy; fraud-detection and velocity-control framework; reconciliation between Apple IAP/Google Play billing events and bank settlement; customer-support dispute log; documented restrictive acceptance of only sanctioned app-store payment channels with no direct-card acceptance outside aggregators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Substance mismatch where the Alberta corporation has no in-province office, staff, or assets despite onboarding as a domestic operating company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office lease or service-agreement in Alberta; designation of an Alberta agent for service of process; local payroll records for at least one Alberta employee or director; board-meeting minutes and corporate resolutions; general-liability and production insurance policies tied to the Alberta head office; operational bank statements showing local Canadian disbursements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant capital injections are routed by SWIFT MT103 (or ISO 20022 pain.001) from the investor's account directly to the Alberta corporation's Canadian bank account. The wire must clearly identify the beneficiary and reference the purpose code for equity investment: under the OECD BPM6/IMF classification, the payment narrative should state 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital Injection into [Company Name]', for tracking under Statistics Canada's direct-investment survey processes. For inbound remittances exceeding CAD 10,000, the bank will capture standard FINTRAC information from the remitter; injections above CAD 75,000 may trigger Statistics Canada reporting, and the relationship manager should be notified in advance to code the entry as foreign direct investment in Canada rather than as trade revenue. Source-of-funds verification requires recent tax returns or financial statements of the investor, a board resolution approving the share issuance, and the executed subscription agreement; funds must move from the investor's own bank account and not from an unrelated third-party wallet.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and production settlements are executed through: (a) SWIFT MT103 bank transfers for creator royalties, studio production payments, and equipment purchases, cleared in USD via CHIPS or Fedwire, in EUR via TARGET2, in CAD via Lynx (Payments Canada's high-value system), and in KRW/HKD via local clearing systems; (b) irrevocable commercial documentary letters of credit (UCP 600) issued by a Canadian Schedule I bank for larger equipment or licensing acquisitions; and (c) multi-currency or foreign-currency accounts (USD, EUR, KRW) to concentrate receipts from Apple and Google and disburse to overseas producers without double FX conversion. All outbound payments are filtered in real time against OSFI/OFAC/UN sanctions lists and Canada's Criminal Code anti-money-laundering protocols; payment instructions must quote the underlying invoice and production contract to satisfy a bank's enhanced due diligence for high-value overseas disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD, KRW/CAD) with tenors of 12 to 24 months under a standard CSA-cleared or bank ISDA master agreement
Foreign-exchange swaps (FX swaps) for short-term liquidity conversion between CAD and USD without taking outright position risk
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCS/XCY) for long-term production-financing cash flows where matched revenue and debt are denominated in different currencies
European-style deliverable FX options (purchased calls and puts) to hedge app-store revenue conversion while preserving upside participation

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-internationalized currencies (e.g., CNY offshore CNH, INR) to hedge subscription revenue from emerging-market app stores, executed through licensed Canadian bank dealing desks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Director of Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Alberta Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CAD 50 late filing fee in addition to the annual return fee; failure to file for two consecutive years renders the corporation liable to administrative dissolution or strike-off by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including Alberta Corporate Tax Schedules and annual financial statement information)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the corporation's taxation year (e.g., December 31 year-end: June 30 of the following calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Federal failure-to-file penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month late (maximum 12 months); repeat default penalty of 10% in certain cases; daily compound interest on unpaid tax; no registry strike-off but enforcement by CRA and risk of director liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (applicable where the corporation is an annual GST/HST remitter)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the GST/HST fiscal year for annual remitters; the fiscal year is generally the calendar year for a December 31 taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of 5%-10% of unpaid GST/HST and daily interest on arrears; penalties for false statements or omissions; no direct administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) minutes and resolutions held at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; no filing with Alberta Corporate Registry, but available for inspection by shareholders and in compliance audits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation; thereafter at least once in every calendar year and no more than 15 months after the preceding AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No monetary filing penalty; directors may be subject to shareholder remedies, court-ordered calling of the meeting, or breach-of-duty liability; persistent default may be considered in a corporate registry enforcement if the annual return remains delinquent.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory annual audit is imposed on a non-distributing Alberta private corporation simply by size or revenue. An auditor is not required if the shareholders pass a unanimous resolution each year to dispense with one. A mandatory audit or auditor appointment generally applies to distributing/offering corporations, or at the request of shareholders holding not less than 5% of the issued shares. For federally incorporated CBCA distributing corporations, audited financial statements must be filed with Corporations Canada.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public-accountable or distributing corporations; Canadian ASPE (Part II CPA Canada Handbook) for private companies; non-distributing private corporations may apply ASPE unless voluntary adoption of IFRS is elected.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not require a separate UBO annual filing form for private corporations; the Alberta Annual Return must be completed with current director and registered-office particulars, and share transfers are recorded in the internal Register of Members. Where the Alberta Corporate Transparency Act applies, the corporation must maintain and update a register of individuals with significant control, and significant-event changes are notified to the director; the register must be accurate as of the date of the annual return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (where applicable)
Minute Book containing shareholders' and directors' resolutions and minutes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if audit dispensed by unanimous shareholder resolution; USD 2,500 - USD 8,000 for a shareholder- or investor-mandated small-entity audit/review

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return filed via CRA e-file / NETFILE (approved tax-prep software); a mandatory electronic filing rule applies to tax preparers; paper filing is restricted to specific cases.
stage_6.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly federal income tax instalments (s.156.1) when net tax owing > CAD 3,000; instalment thresholds based on prior-year tax liability.
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (s.150(1)); for a December 31 year-end, the filing due date is June 30 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate legal name, CRA business number, Alberta Corporate Registry number, status of majority Canadian-controlled/foreign-controlled (CCPC vs. non-CCPC).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporation must indicate the country of residence and the Canadian permanent-establishment address; if no Canadian operations, mark the foreign-incorporated box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue lines (digital subscriptions, in-app purchases, licensing and distribution of micro-drama content); cost lines (content acquisition, streaming bandwidth, Apple IAP/Google Play commission charges, Stripe processor fees).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue reasonably attributed to a Canadian permanent establishment; foreign-source subscription revenue is excluded from Part I income unless it is derived from carrying on business in Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation of basic Part I tax on taxable income: 15% net federal rate (after 10% provincial abatement); deduction for SBD, SR&ED credits, and CAVCO/FTVC credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies do not claim the CCPC small-business deduction; federal tax rate of 15% applies to Canadian PE-attributable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apportionment of taxable income between Alberta and other provinces by permanent-establishment formula; Alberta general rate 8%; 2% for eligible CCPC on first CAD 500,000 active business income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate taxable income to Alberta if the principal PE is in Alberta; otherwise, allocate based on the formula in the Regulations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, address, residence status and withheld totals for dividends, royalties and interest paid to non-resident shareholders/licensors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This schedule supports the payer's obligation to withhold 25% on each non-resident payment or the treaty-reduced rate where a valid TRC is obtained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 88 / 89 – SR&ED and Production Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Investment tax credits for qualifying R&D in streaming algorithms and Alberta production-colouration credits; CAVCO film/video production tax credit percentage.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-resident corporations generally are ineligible unless the R&D is performed in Canada through a PE; separate CAVCO certification files apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of non-arm's length transactions between the Alberta company and the related-party licensors, sub-licensees, or foreign distribution affiliates, exceeding CAD 1,000,000 in the year (s. 233.1(4)(a)).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The T106 is filed by the Canadian payer; the amount threshold applies to the aggregate of all non-arm's length international transactions.

stage_6.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing: 5% of the balance owing plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months (federal); Alberta levies a parallel penalty under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act. Repeated/late filings within 3 years: a further 10% penalty. Gross negligence (s.163(2)): 50% of the understated tax. Information return (T106) penalty: CAD 24 per day, capped at CAD 2,400; CAD 100 per day, up to CAD 25,000, if wilfully failed; s.233.3(j) penalties can apply per month.
